<entry id="S00610">
<head-word>קוֹרְיָיס</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (corius, corium) 
<italic>leather, skin, bark</italic>; כלי ק' leather garments, 
<italic>working clothes</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Sabb. XVII, 16
<sup>a</sup> bot. מהו לטלטל כ' ק' וכ' is it permitted to handle working garments on the Sabbath? Gen. R. s. 49, beg. שמותם … לכ' ק' וכ' the names of the wicked are like leather garments; as long as you use them, they wear well; when you let them lie, they rot. Koh. R. to II, 17 נתעטף בכ' ק' שלו he wrapped himself in his working clothes. Deut. R. s. 7 (ref. to Deut. XXIX, 4) (כלום) כ' ק' וכ' were leather garments carried with the Israelites out of Egypt (that they did not wear out)?; Cant. R. to IV, 11; Pesik. B’shall., p. 92
<sup>a</sup>, a. Yalk. Deut. 850 קוריות (read: קוֹרְיוּם); Yalk. Ps. 691; Midr. Till. to Ps. XXIII קוריים (ed. Bub. קואים, read: קוריום).—[Gen. R. s. 71 Ar.; Esth. R. to I, 10, v. קוֹרִיִּים.—Koh. R. to III, 11 שפעת ק', read: קוֹרִים, v. שִׁפְעָה I, a. קוֹרָה III.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00640">
<head-word>קוֹרְקְבָן</head-word>

<pos> m.</pos>

<sense>
<definition> (= קבקב'; cmp. קוֹבַע, כּוֹבַע) 
<italic>the thick muscular stomach of birds, craw</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. III, 3. Ib. 6 (among the characteristics of clean birds) קוֹרְקְבָנוֹ נקלף whose craw peels easily; Tosef. ib. III (IV), 22; Ḥull. 61
<sup>a</sup> וקוּרְקְבָנָן נקלף (not וקורקבן); Yalk. Lev. 537 וקרקבנו (corr. acc.); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קָרְקְבָנִין</plural-form> (with sing. meaning). Tosef. l. c. 16 באלו … אמרו בק' וכ' by these intestines are meant: the craw, the liver, and the heart. Sifra Vayiḳra, N’dabah, ch. VIII, Par. 7.—In gen. 
<italic>stomach</italic> (= הֶמְסֵס). Ber. 61
<sup>b</sup> top ק' טוחן the stomach (of man) grinds. Sabb. 152
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Koh. XII, 4) בשביל ק' שאינו טוחן on account of the stomach’s failing to grind.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
